list.listitem: NAFLD is the most common cause of elevated liver enzymes in adults. C
The primary risk factors for NAFLD are central obesity, diabetes, hypertriglyceridemia and metabolic syndrome. C
The primary treatment for NAFLD is weight loss, treatment of associated conditions such as diabetes, hyperlipidmemia and avoidance of hepatotoxic drugs. B

Medications used to treat diabetes and hyperlipidemia have demonstrated an improvement in liver enzyme levels and histology, but there are no studies to support demonstrating improved patient-oriented outcomes. C

Steatosis alone in the absence of significant fibrosis generally has a benign course. For patients with NAFLD, the risk of death, ascites, hepatocellular cancer, and encephalopathy are all increased in persons with F3 or F4 fibrosis. B

background.definition: Nonalcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD) represents a spectrum of disorders characterized by predominantly macrovesicular hepatic steatosis in the absence of significant alcohol consumption and no competing cause for steatosis. Nonalcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) is a more severe form with inflammation and varying degrees of fibrosis in addition to fatty infiltration. Metabolic dysfunction-associated fatty liver disease "(MAFLD)" is the term suggested in 2020 to refer to fatty liver disease related to systemic metabolic dysregulation by the international experts.

list.listitem: The reported incidence varies considerably depending on the definition and population. The estimated global incidence of NAFLD is 47 cases per 1,000 population. In an English study, the incidence was 29 cases of NAFLD per 100,000 person-years, while Japanese studies show rates of 31 to 86 cases per 1000 person-years. Greater use of screening and office-based ultrasound in Japan may lead to ascertainment bias.

The estimated global prevalence of NAFLD among adults is 32% and is higher among males (40%) compared to females (26%). Recent meta analysis of pooled data from 72 studies (1,030,160 individuals) estimated that the global prevalence of NAFLD in adults was 32%.

The overall prevalence of NAFLD in the U.S. is estimated to be 24%. Prevalence are higher in Hispanic Americans and lower in African Americans. NASH, a subset of NAFLD, affects 1.5% to 6.5% of the US population., ,

Predictive modeling using NHANES data base (2017-2018) showed age-adjusted prevalence of NAFLD and of NAFLD with F0–F1 and F2–F4 fibrosis was 25.3%, 18.9%, and 4.4%, respectively in the overall population, and 54.6%, 32.6%, and 18.3% in those with T2DM.
In individuals with obesity, the prevalence ranges from 50-90%, More than 90% of morbidly obese individuals have NAFLD.

Lean NAFLD should be diagnosed in individuals with NAFLD and body mass index <25 kg/m2 (non-Asian race) or body mass index <23 kg/m2 (Asian race). They should be evaluated routinely for comorbid conditions, such as type 2 diabetes mellitus, dyslipidemia, and hypertension.

In diabetics the pooled prevalance of NALFD is 59.6%, however the range noted was high (29.6%-87.1%). Specifically In Type1 DM, Pooled NAFLD prevalence was dependent on specific diagnostic modality and NAFLD definition; vary from 19.3% (95% CI, 12.3%-27.5%), increasing to 22.0% (95% CI, 13.9%-31.2%) in adults only.

Using US data from NHANES 2009 to 2012, the prevalence of NASH associated cirrhosis is 0.178%. The prevalence of NAFLD with advanced fibrosis is 1.75%. Both of these rates increased compared with 1999 to 2002.

NAFLD progressing to NASH is the most common cause of cryptogenic cirrhosis (cirrhosis not explained by hepatitis, alcohol abuse, toxins, biliary tract disease, congenital disease, or autoimmune disease). Although cirrhosis is a rare complication of NAFLD, it is becoming more common as rates of diabetes and morbid obesity increase.

NASH patients has higher rates of hepatocellular carcinoma than the general population and have an annual rate that is 12 times higher than patients with NAFLD (5.77 vs 0.44 events per 1000 person-years).

NAFLD‐related deaths in U.S. adults are increasing and during the study period, the age standardized death rate (ASDR) for among NAFLD 353,234 decedents increased by 15%. NAFLD patients had significantly increased overall mortality (16.9 vs. 28.6/1000 person-years).

Hospitalized Cardio Vascular Disease patients with NAFLD were at a significantly higher risk of all-cause mortality than non-NAFLD patients (adjusted hazard ratio of 2.08 [95% CI, 1.56-2.59], P <.001).
There are the associated risk factors for NAFLD: Obesity, Diabetes, Hypertriglycerdemia, Low HDL, Genetic predisposition and certain diet like high fructose corn syrup or fructose.

Other conditions associated with fatty liver includes: Drugs, Toxins, Parental Nutrition, Lipodystrophy, Hepatitis C (Genotype 3), Inborn errors of metabolism (i.e. Wilson's disease), Alochol use ( "significant" is defined more than 21 drinks per week in men and 14 drinks per week in women).
The pathophysiology is poorly understood.

Insulin resistance leads to a build-up of free fatty acids in the liver. Increased accumulation of lipids in hepatocytes are due to increased production or reduced clearance of hepatic triglycerides or fatty acids.
Oxidative stress may lead to mitochondrial dysfunction and the development of inflammation (steatohepatitis).

Single-nucleotide polymorphisms, in particular the patatin-like phospholipase domain-containing protein 3 (PNPLA3) gene which encodes the I148M protein variant, are associated with increased hepatic fat. A meta analysis of 20 studies demonstrated a significant increased association between PNPLA3 rs738,409 and NAFLD.

PNPLA3 rs738409 G-allele may modulate the effect of specific dietary nutrients on risk of fibrosis.High-carbohydrate (% of energy/d) intake was positively associated (adjusted [Adj.] odds ratio [OR]: 1.03, P <0.01), whereas higher n-3 polyunsaturated fatty acids (n-3 PUFAs) (g/d) (Adj. OR: 0.17, P <0.01), isoflavones (mg/d) (Adj. OR: 0.74, P = 0.049), methionine (mg/d) (Adj. OR: 0.32, P <0.01), and choline (mg/d) (Adj. OR: 0.32, P <0.01) intakes were inversely associated with increased risk of significant fibrosis (stage of fibrosis ≥2).

A positive relationship exists between dietary carbohydrates and liver fat content among UK Biobank participants. Fibre, non-free sugars, and starch from whole grains were inversely associated with liver fat, whereas starch from refined grains showed a positive association with liver fat.
A meta-analysis of 21 articles established an association between the progression of NALFD in the Asian population and infection with H pylori.
There are no recommendations regarding screening for NAFLD or NASH for the general population.

Guidelines from the AASLD, ACG and AGA specifically recommend against screening for NAFLD or NASH. Current recommendations include a no-screening strategy (AASLD/NICE) and screening directed toward a high-risk population (EASL).

NAFLD should be considered in lean individuals with metabolic diseases (such as type 2 diabetes mellitus, dyslipidemia, and hypertension), elevated liver biochemical tests, or incidentally noted hepatic steatosis.

Guidelines from the AGA based largely on expert opinion recommend that for patients with NAFLD and non-invasive tests that suggest advanced fibrosis (F3) or cirrhosis (F4), one should consider regular surveillance for hepatocellular carcinoma and esophageal varices. These patients should also undergo serial liver stiffness measurement; vibration controlled transient elastography; or MR elastography.
Suspect NAFLD in obese patients with elevated aminotransferases who consume minimal alcohol. C
Rule out hepatitis, hemochromatosis, and autoimmune hepatitis and confirm diagnosis with ultrasound in nondrinking patients. C
Clinical rules have been developed to predict which patients have NASH and which patients with NASH have significant fibrosis. C

Differential.Differential_Features: AST usually greater than ALT; history of alcohol abuse.
Positive viral serologies; steatosis with HepC, but not HepB.
Antinuclear antibodies and antismooth muscle antibodies; no steatosis.
Increased serum ferritin and transferrin saturation; no steatosis.

list.listitem: Most patients with NAFLD are asymptomatic.
There are no pathognomonic signs of NAFLD or NASH.
Hepatomegaly is the most common physical finding.
Individuals with cirrhosis from NAFLD will have findings similar to cirrhosis of other causes.
The AST/ALT ratio is usually less than 1 in NAFLD and greater than 1 in alcohol-related liver disease. An AST/ALT ratio greater than 1 in an individual with NAFLD suggests more severe disease. :
Ultrasound is the best initial test to confirm the diagnosis due to the excellent specificity. The sensitivity increased to 100% and the specificity to 90% when there was > or =20% of fat.
B mode ultrasonography (B-USG) showed a sensitivity of 83.4%, specificity of 81.0%, and AUC of 0.822 in diagnosing mild liver steatosis.
The residual attenuation coefficient (RAC), one of the calibrated US parameter can detect steatosis with AUC of 0.97 and stages steatosis accurately.

The combination of dispersion slope, attenuation coefficient, and shear-wave speed in a Multiparametric Ultrasound of the liver are useful in diagnosis of NASH. Measurements of hepatic steatosis using Ultrasound Derived Fat Fraction (UDFF) show strong agreement with measurements by MRI proton-density fat fraction ( PDFF).

Serum indices (NAFLD fibrosis score and Fibrosis-4 score) and imaging techniques (transient elastography and magnetic resonance elastography) may be used as alternatives to liver biopsy for fibrosis staging and patient follow-up. These tests can be performed at the time of diagnosis and repeated at intervals of 6 months to 2 years, depending on fibrosis stage and the patient's response to intervention.

Compensated advanced liver disease (advanced fibrosis and cirrhosis) secondary to NAFLD can be identified by two step strategy of using lower liver stiffness measures cut off (8/12 kPa) and modeling based on presence of diabetes, serum AST levels.

An individual patient data meta-analysis with 5735 patients concluded that vibration controlled transient elastography > 7.4 was moderately accurate for diagnosis of advanced fibrosis. (LR+ 2.3, LR- 0.2).

MRI and magnetic resonance spectroscopy may be useful for differentiating stages of NAFLD. Attenuation coefficient accuracy varied among US devices when using liver fat quantification with the MRI-derived proton density fat fraction (PDFF).
MR fingerprinting derived metrics showed high diagnostic performance in differentiaing between moderte and severe liver disease, and may correlate with pathological grade.

Liver stiffness assessed by Magnetic Resonance Elastography (MRE) is associated with liver related outcomes with hazard ratio of 11 for MRE of 5 to 8 kPa and 15.9 for MRE of f ≥ 8 kPa. MRE + Fibrosis-4 (MEFIB index defined as positive when MRE ≥3.3 kPa and Fibrosis-4 ≥1.6 had a strong association with the hepatic decomensation [ hazard ratio of 20.6 (95% CI: 10.4-40.8, P < .001)] and a negative MEFIB had a high negative predictive value for the same with 99.1% at 5 years.

The clinical utility of these indices such as Hepatic steatosis index, Framingham steatosis index, Dallas steatosis index and ALT method in diagnosing hepatic steatosis in the absence of imaging in real-world settings is supported.

The FAST(Fibroscan AST) score can be used as a noninvasive screening tool mainly for excluding the diagnosis of progressive NASH. in One Brazilian study, the FAST cut-off of 0.35, the S and NPV to rule out NASH + NAS ≥ 4 + F ≥ 2 were 78.8% and 87.8%, respectively.

A meta-analysis to identify the diagnostic accuracy of fibrotic NASH showed that the Fibroscan AST (FAST) score's pooled sensitivity was 89%, the pooled specificity was 89%, with LR+ 8 and LR- 0.12. Given an overall rate of fibrosis of 28%, the negative predictive value was 92%, and the positive predictive value was 65%.

The use of liver biopsy is controversial. You may consider it for individuals suspected of more severe disease (ie, those who are morbidly obese, have diabetes, have an AST/ALT ratio >1, or if the clinical rules below suggest higher likelihood of fibrosis) or if the diagnosis is uncertain. It is not recommended for patients with hepatic steatosis detected on ultrasound or CT but who are asymptomatic.

Fibrosis ≥F2 along with NAS ≥4 only present in a few cases of NAFLD. Transient elastography and FIB-4 are useful to select patients at risk for fibrosis for liver biopsy. Liver stiffness measurement, LSM (OR 2.3 per doubling of value; CI 1.3-4.4, p = .005) and FIB-4 (OR 2.3 per doubling of value; CI 1.2-4.4, p = .012) were significant predictors for fibrosis ≥F2 and are useful to select patients at risk for fibrosis for liver biopsy.

It is also important to rule out other causes of steatosis and chronic liver disease, such as infection, hemochromatosis (high ferritin, increased iron saturation, C282Y HFE mutation), and autoimmune disease..
Serum markers are less reliable in predicting advanced fibrosis in NAFLD patients with Chronic Hepatitis B; AST to Platelet Ratio is the most accurate predictor of the absence of advanced fibrosis.
Sex-specific metabolomics biomarkers of NAFLD are superior predictors of high Hepatic Fat Fraction (HFF).

There is a possbility of Small Density Low Density Lipoprotien (sLDL) as new biomarker for NAFLD. Blood levels of sdLDL level in NAFLD patients have a positive correlation with the Controlled Attenuation Parameter (CAP) value and liver stiffness measured by Transient Elastography, which indicate the degree of hepatic steatosis and fibrosis.

Non invasive biomarker such a s flow cytometry measured perilipin-2 (PLIN2) and RAB14 in peripheral blood CD14+CD16- monocytes is accurate, sensitive and specific in diagnosing the presence and severity of NASH or liver fibrosis.

Elevated serum levels of S100A6 or calcyclin, inhibits glucose-stimulated insulin secretion (GSIS) from β cells may serve as a biomarker in identifying patients with NAFLD with a heightened risk of developing β-cell dysfunction.

Diagnostic performances of indices such as Fatty Liver Index (FLI), Hepatic Steatosis Index (HSI), Lipid Accumulation Product (LAP), and Dallas Steatosis Index (DSI) are comparable for detection of Fatty liver Disease with alcohol consumption <50 g/day and with different binge-drinking behaviour.

A meta-analysis of 4 database suggested that currently availalable nonivasive tests such as (Fib-4) and NAFLD fibrosis score (NFS) have a limited performance in identifying advance fibrosis among subjects with NAFLD. However, sequential combinations of markers such as Fibrosis-4 Index (FIB-4), liver stiffness measurement by vibration controlled transient elastography (LSM-VCTE) with a lower cut-off to rule-out advanced fibrosis and a higher cut-off to rule-in cirrhosis can reduce the need for liver biopsies.
Clinical rules have been developed to predict the likelihood of severe fibrosis in patients with NASH.
The HAIR score identifies the risk of NASH in obese patients.
What is the probability of fibrosis in patients with non-alcoholic fatty liver using the NAFLD Fibrosis Score.
In a patient with suspected NAFLD or NASH, first assess for viral hepatitis with serology and rule out significant alcohol use.
Also consider serum transferrin saturation and serum ferritin to rule out hemochromatosis and ANA to rule out autoimmune hepatitis.
See for a suggested approach to the patient.

Patients who are overweight and obesity, who have NAFLD should consider a weight-loss program; weight loss should proceed at one to two pounds per week. More rapid weight loss, particularly following bariatric surgery, may exacerbate NASH. C
Medical therapy should be directed at the correction of risk factors for NASH (insulin resistance, hyperlipidemia). C
Statin medications should not be withheld because of mild elevation of transaminases (ie, less than 3 times the upper limit of normal) in individuals with NAFLD. C

There are currently no FDA-approved medications for the treatment of NAFLD, but drugs may be considered in appropriate clinical setting especially to treat associated comorbidities with potential benefit in NAFLD. However according to EASL guidelines, drug therapy should be implemented in patients with progressive NASH (bridging fibrosis and cirrhosis); early stage NASH with high risk for disease progression (increased ALT, presence of metabolic syndrome and diabetes mellitus, age >50 years) and active NASH with high necroinflammatory activities.

A meta analysis of 7 RCT studied the effect of pilglitazone showed improved liver enzymes, steatosis, and histology in both diabetic and nondiabetic NAFLD patients. Women respond better than men.. However, thiazolidinediones cause significant weight gain. While a network meta-analysis found that they are associated with an increased likelihood of resolution of NASH, a second meta-analysis concluded that thiazolidinediones had no effect on the development of fibrosis in patients with NASH.
Oral pioglitazone 30 mg daily may be considered in lean persons with biopsy-confirmed nonalcoholic steatohepatitis without cirrhosis.
Oral dapagliflozin, a sodium-glucose cotransporter 2 inhibitors, might be more beneficial than pioglitazone in reducing the fatty liver index in patients with NAFLD in a small study.

A double blind placebo-controlled phase 2 trial of GLP-1 agonist subcutaneous semalgludide involving patients with NASH resulted in resolution of NASH with no worsening of fibrosis was 40% in the 0.1-mg group, 36% in the 0.2-mg group, 59% in the 0.4-mg group, and 17% in the placebo group (P <0.001 for semaglutide 0.4 mg vs. placebo).

Observational studies has shown a possible protective role of statin treatment against NAFLD progression to HCC. Statin treatment was associated with significantly reduced NAS and FIB-4 scores at the end of 1 year follow up in a study involving 604 military personal with NAFLD/NASH.

However many patients with NASH otherwise qualify for statins. The safety of statin use in the group was assessed in a a postdoc analysis of statin use during a randomized controlled trial of Pioglitazone on NASH progression. In this study 86 patient's with biopsy-proven NASH who also had glucose intolerance or diabetes were on statins and were followed for up to 36 months. When compared to patients with biopsy-proven NASH who were not on statins, no major difference were noted between the 2 groups with regards to increases in plasma transaminases. However, all of these studies are poor and at high risk of bias, and use of statins is not recommended as a treatment for NASH or NAFLD.

Metformin, ursodeoxycholic acid, dipeptidyl peptidase-4, statins, and silymarin are well studied in NASH and should not be used as a treatment for NASH as they do not offer a meaningful histological benefit.

Obetichoic acid (a bile acid derivative which when bound to farnesoid X nuclear receptor improves insulin sensitivity, and decreases hepatic gluconeogeneisis and circulating triglycerides) given 25 mg daily was more effective in improving liver histopathology (45% vs. 21%) among patients with NASH than was placebo in a 72 week randomized controlled trial among 931 patients with NASH or NAFLD with fibrosis. However pruritis occurred in 23% of the active treatment group compared to 6% in the palcebo group.

Aldafermin, an engineered FGF19 analog in patients in NASH results significant reduction in absolute liver fat content (reduction of 7.7%) compared with placebo (reduction of 2.7%; difference, reduction of 5.0%; 95% CI, reduction of 8.0%-1.9%; P = .002).
Polypill (pill containing aspirin, atorvastatin, hydrochlorothiazide, and valsartan ) is safe and effective preventing major cardiovascular event in patients with NAFLD in a 5 year followup RCT.
Ezetimibe in combination with statin (ESSENTIAL study) reduces the liver fat by MRI-PDFF (mean difference: 3.2%; p = 0.020) than statin alone monotherapy.

Pegozafermin is a fibroblast growth factor 21 analogue. In a Phase 2 RCT with 222 patients, it improved fibrosis (reduction by >= 1 stage on a 4 point scale) in 22% to 27% of patients given the active drug and 7% in those given placebo. However, patient-oriented outcomes were not evaluated and the drug has not been FDA approved.

Consider gastric bypass for morbidly obese individuals. A Cochrane review failed to find any RCTs of bariatric surgery for patients with NASH; although cohort studies report some benefit in steatosis or inflammation scores, four described some deterioration in the degree of fibrosis.

Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB) and laparoscopic sleeve gastrectomy (LSG) are the most common method performed results in significant reduction in the incidence of major adverse cardiovascular events (OR 0.49) and resolution of NASH in 2/3 of patients.

BRAVES ( Bariatric-metabolic surgery vs Lifestyle intervention + medical care) trial, a multicenter RCT showed the cacluated resolution of NASH is 3·60 times greater (95% CI 2·19-5·92; p<0·0001) in the Roux-en-Y gastric bypass group and 3·67 times greater (2·23-6·02; p<0·0001) in the sleeve gastrectomy group compared with in the lifestyle modification group.
A randomized clinical trial showed sleeve gastrectomy to cause less transient deterioration of liver function than those undergoing Roux-en-Y gastric bypass.
High-dose digestive enzymes administration prevented the development of NAFLD after pancreaticoduodenectomy (PD) compared to normal dose.
DJBL ( Duodenal-Jejunal Bypass Linear), a medical device used to treat DM2 and Obesity in addition to intensive medical care improved fatty liver disease markers.

Similar liver fat fraction reduction observed after sleeve gastrectomy (SG) and Roux-en-Y gastric bypass (RYGB) from surgery to 1-year followup, but Enhanced liver Fibrosis (ELF) score remained stable, even got worse in 18% of patients.
Diet:
Decrease in Intrahepatic lipid content was found on 6 weeks of fructose restriction (FRUITLESS) in a small double blinded RCT.
Soy diet may benefit to reduce insulin resistance for NAFLD.
Low Carb High Fat (LCHF) diet compared to High Carb Low Fat (HCLF) diet had greater improvement in HbA1 C and weight loss in Diabetic NAFLD.
Absolute reduction of fatty liver is greater with diet based on fresh water fish compared to fresh water fish + red meat (-4.89% vs -1.83%, P = 0.032) in an small RCT.
Fruit rich diet (FRD), consumption of fruits more than 4 servings per day exacerbate steatosis, dyslipidemia and glycemic control in NAFLD patients.

Among 100 obese Chinese women with NALFD and metabolic syndrome, daily consumption of 220g per day of yogurt was associated with improved markers of disease activity when compared to 220g pe day of milk.
Nutrional Supplement and Vitamins:
Treatment with vitamin E is associated with improved histology in patients with biopssy-proven NASH and is recommended by guidelines, but evidence of improved patient-oriented outcomes is lacking.
Vitamin E is not recommended for patients with NASH and co-morbid diabetes, NAFLD without liver biopsy, NASH cirrhosis, or cryptogenic cirrhosis.
Vitamin D and resveratrol have been found to have no meaningful effect on NALFD.
One observational study involing 65 patients with NAFLD with hypovitaminosis D, have a low response rate to Vitamin D supplementation.
Dietary supplementation with L-carnitine may have role since it inhibits β-oxidation, improves mitochondrial dysfunction, and reduces insulin resistance to ameliorate NAFLD.
Betaine, a nutritional supplement, did not improve steatosis, but may protect against worsening steatosis.
Life style modifcations:
Weight loss is recommended. A loss of at least 3% to 5% of body weight may improve fatty liver, but more substantial weight loss of 10% or more is often needed
After 6 months of treatment with CPAP alone on NAFLD patients with OSA, did not improve hepatic steatosis and fibrosis in a RCT (n = 120).

A meta ananlysis of 14 studies includes patients with NAFLD showed significant treatment response (MRI response odds ratio 3.73, 95% confidence interval 1.34-10.41, P = 0.010) to an exercise dose of at least 750 metabolic equivalents of task-min/wk (150 minutes of brisk walk/week).
High intensity interval training (HIT) is safe, efficacious in terms of improving the exercise capacity and peripheral insulin sensitivity in biopsy proven NASH.
Higher physical activity (volume and intensity) and effort on diety quality are associated with low cardiovascular mortality in adults with NAFLD.

In a small RCT of obese diabetic patients with NALFD, exercise (either high intensity interval training or moderate-intensity continuous training) was associated with decreased hepatic fat and visceral lipids vs a non-exercising control group.
Novel therapy:

AXA1125 and AXA1957 are novel, orally administered endogenous metabolic modulator,showed multitargeted activity on relevant NAFLD pathways espcially AXA1125 demonstrated the greatest activity over 16 weeks.

TVB-2640, a fatty acid synthase inhibitor, reduced liver fat by 9.6% in the 25-mg cohort (n = 30; least squares mean: -15.5%; 95% confidence interval, -31.3 to -0.23; P = .053), and 28.1% in the 50-mg cohort (n = 28; least squares mean: -28.0%; 95% confidence interval, -44.5 to -11.6; P = .001) and improved biochemical, inflammatory, and fibrotic biomarkers after 12 weeks.

1200-mg of Lanifibranor, a pan-PPAR (peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor) agonist in a phase 2 b trial showed decrease of at least 2 points in the SAF-A score without worsening of fibrosis compared to placebo.

Fetal Microbiota Transplantation (FMT) did not improve IR as measured by HOMA-IR or hepatic proton density fat fraction (PDFF) but did have the potential to reduce small intestinal permeability in patients with NAFLD.

Consider referral to a specialist when the clinical picture suggests more severe disease, such as patients whose enzymes fail to improve with weight loss, morbidly obese patients, those with an AST/ALT ratio greater than 1, and if the clinical prediction rules suggest a higher likelihood of fibrosis in patients with NASH.

Steatosis alone in the absence of significant fibrosis generally has a benign course. For patients with NAFLD, the risk of death, ascites, hepatocellular cancer, and encephalopathy are all increased in persons with F3 or F4 fibrosis. B
Some patients with NASH progress to cirrhosis, but reliable data on the incidence of progression are lacking. C
Risk factors for more severe disease include morbid obesity, diabetes, and an AST/ALT ratio greater than 1. C
Steatosis alone in the absence of significant fibrosis generally has a benign course.

A large multicenter study identified 1773 adults with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease (NAFLD). Adverse outcomes were significantly more common in patients with F3 or F4 fibrosis compared to those with F0 to F2 fibrosis: encephalopathy (0.02 for F0 to F2 vs. 0.75 for F3 vs. 2.39 for F4 per 100 person years), variceal hemorrhage (0.00 vs. 0.06 vs. 0.70/100 person-years), ascites (0.04 vs. 0.52 vs. 1.20/100 person-years), and hepatocellular cancer (0.04 vs. 0.34 vs. 0.14/100 person-years) All cause mortality was also higher: 0.32/100 person-years for F0 to F2, versus 0.89 for F3 and 1.76 for F4.
1/3 of children with NAFLD in association with increasing obesity, ALT levels and loss of glucose homeostasis had histological progression within 2 years.

A Swedish study of 36 patients with biopsy proven NAFLD and followed for 27 years revealed that 9 patients (25%) were diagnosed with cirrhosis, and had a higher mortality rate (58.3%) compared to a control group (33.8%), and that hepatocellular cancer accounted for 23.8% of all deaths.

A study following 289 patients with biopsy-proven NAFLD found that during a median 12 year follow-up, patients with non-alcoholic steatohepatitis (NASH) had a higher risk of liver-related death than those with non-NASH NAFLD (aHR 9.2; 95% CI, 2.1-9.9). Increasing age and co-morbid T2DM were also risk factors for a bad outcome.
Presence of diabetes drives the progression of NAFLD to severe liver disease such as NASH, Cirrhosis and HCC.
Genetically predicted NAFLD was associated with a higher risk of developing PCOS (OR per one-unit log odds increase in NAFLD: 1.10, 95% CI: 1.02-1.18; P = 0.013).
Individuals with NAFLD have a slightly higher mortality than the general population (HR of 0.92)..
Fatty liver is the one of the common reason for discarding the liver graft and GGT poorly correlete with microvascular steatosis.

Although weight loss and various medications have been shown to reduce transaminase levels, decrease liver fat content, and improve histologic scoring, none have yet been proven to affect morbidity or mortality.
There are no specific guidelines for monitoring liver enzymes, steatosis, or liver histology and there are no data that define the effects of the treatment of fatty liver on morbidity or mortality.
The relative change in the MRI-based proton-density fat fraction (PDFF) at week 4 was highly predictive of the treatment response estimated by using the week 12 MRI-based PDFF.
NAFLD is generally caused by the same conditions that cause an increased risk for heart disease and stroke.
Most cases of NAFLD do not cause serious health problems.
Rarely, some patients develop cirrhosis; this is more common in individuals who are morbidly obese and have diabetes.
There are no specific treatments for NAFLD, but the treatment of risk factors for cardiovascular disease—specifically diabetes, elevated lipids, and obesity—may improve NAFLD.
NAFLD is commonly found in obese children. The estimated prevalence of NAFLD was 26.0%.
As is the case with adults, most children with NAFLD are asymptomatic.

Levels of serum marker such as cathepsin D (CatD), one of the lysosomal enzyme are inversly proportional to the presence of hepatic inflammation, and may be a useful marker in children to distinguish hepatic inflammation from hepatitic steatosis without inflammation.
Primary treatment is diet and exercise.
Although metformin has been proved to have an excellent therapeutic effect on children's NAFLD, attention has to be paid on the sideeffects.

Among 64 children (average age 13) with NASH, omega-3 fatty acid supplementation was associated with improved AST (28 vs. 39 U/L) and gamma-glutamyl transpeptidase (26 vs. 35 U/L) but not with liver hyperechogenecity on ultrasound nor the number of patients with an ALT decrease of >0.3 times the upper limit of normal.
Enhanced liver Fibrosis (ELF) score, a non invasive test is useful to monitor the treatment response in children with NAFLD.
Elevated serum hyaluronic acid may be useful for predicting fibrosis in adults and children with NAFLD.
